correctness.rationale: Hilbert barycentric variance on the m-point part and any two-point part gives C^2 >= 2(m-1)/m+1 exactly. Orthogonal simplex and antipodal vectors attain lower bound. For each pair class, equality in both variance bounds forces common centroid, all within-class edges two, all cross distances C; subtracting ± norms enforces pair directions orthogonal to simplex. Between different pairs, squared distances 2±2 inner product enforce |inner product| <= min(1/2,(C^2-2)/2)=(m-2)/(2m). Volume packing supplies d>=Omega(log t), Rademacher/union bound O_m(log t), and Welch Gram rank gives d(7,1/6)>=6, attained by regular 7-simplex in dimension6. Independently reconstructed Gram example m=3,t=7 with exact squared distortion 7/3 and optimal affine dimension8. Finite examples do not replace rigidity proof.

value.rationale: The same constant distortion conceals a sharp dimension-rigidity transition from linear number of antipodal parts to logarithmic dimension when the large part grows from size two to three. The complete characterization of all optimizers through spherical lines is a structural classification of natural multipartite shortest-path metrics, beyond a known two-class lower bound.
